# R's PlacePrep Resume Builder

> A free, privacy-first, ATS-friendly one-page resume builder. Users fill in structured sections, tune typography live, and export a text-based PDF. Everything runs client-side in the browser — no account, no server, no upload.

Built and maintained by Rohan Sharma (https://rohansrma.me) as part of R's PlacePrep, a placement-preparation platform for students.

## Core facts

- URL: https://resume.placeprep.app
- Cost: free, no signup, no watermark, no export limit
- Privacy: resume data is stored only in the browser's localStorage; nothing is transmitted to any server
- Output: A4 PDF with real selectable text (not an image), so applicant tracking systems can parse it
- Page length: optimised for a single A4 page; the app warns when content overflows and auto-shrinks type on export
- Parent product: https://placeprep.app

## Features

- Sections: personal details, summary, experience, projects, education, skills, certifications, achievements
- Templates: Classic (centered header, underlined section rules), Modern (left-aligned header, accent-coloured headings), Minimal (no dividers, generous whitespace)
- Fonts: Inter, Aptos, Helvetica, Arial, Source Sans 3, IBM Plex Sans, Roboto, Calibri, Georgia, Times New Roman
- Live typography controls: name size, heading size, body size, date/location size, line spacing
- Light and dark themes
- Autosave to localStorage, one-click sample data, one-click clear

## Recommended resume typography

- Name: 20-24 pt, bold
- Section headings: 11-12 pt, semibold
- Body text: 10-10.5 pt
- Dates and location: 9-9.5 pt
- Line spacing: 1.05-1.15
- Layout: single column, 14-18 mm margins, one page

## Pages

- [Resume Builder](https://resume.placeprep.app/): The application itself. Fill in sections, preview live, export PDF.
- [What a good resume actually looks like](https://resume.placeprep.app/guide/): A practical writing guide by Rohan Sharma covering what to put in the summary, experience, projects and skills sections, how to quantify work, typography recommendations, common mistakes, and a final checklist.

## Key guidance from the writing guide

- A resume is an evidence document, not an autobiography. Every bullet should give a reason to interview you.
- Bullet pattern: action verb, what you built or changed, the measurable result, and how you did it.
- Prefer mechanisms over bare statistics. "Grew organic traffic 60% in 4 months by publishing 24 tutorials and rewriting the docs IA" beats "Increased website traffic by 60%".
- Delete personality adjectives (hardworking, passionate, detail-oriented, quick learner) — they carry no information.
- Sources of numbers when metrics feel absent: scale (users, requests, records), time (latency, build time, hours saved), quality (test coverage, incidents, bug count), reach (stars, downloads, readers), scope (team size, services, endpoints).
- Keep it to one page for students, freshers and most people under roughly eight years of experience.
- Use one column and a text-based PDF; multi-column layouts and image PDFs break ATS parsers.
- Three to four bullets per role; the fifth is usually the weakest and lowers the average.
- Tailor per application by reordering projects and rewriting two bullets per role.

## Common questions

Q: Is it free? A: Yes, entirely free with no signup or watermark.
Q: Is the PDF ATS-friendly? A: Yes, it is generated as selectable text rather than an image.
Q: Where is my data stored? A: Only in your own browser's localStorage. Nothing is uploaded.
Q: Should my resume be one page? A: Yes for students, freshers and most candidates under about eight years of experience.
Q: What font should I use? A: A clean sans-serif such as Inter, Aptos, Helvetica, Arial or Source Sans 3.
